text:
maria: rolled out the adaptive KV-prefetch + dynamic microbatcher to prod @ 10:12 PT. did a gradual ramp, canary was green.

deploy-bot: deploy started: commit b3f9c2a -> prod | canary=5% -> 50% -> 100% | sha b3f9c2a | duration 00:18:24

alex: quick numbers from the perf dashboard after 30m of 100% traffic: p50 tokens latency -11%, p95 -32%, p99 -27%, cost per 1k tokens -22%. rough summary below.

alex: ```
before: {p50: 85ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 450ms, cost_per_1k: $0.042} 
after:  {p50: 76ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 330ms, cost_per_1k: $0.033}
```

jen: nice! do we have any workload breakdowns? long-context vs short-context?

alex: short-context (<=128) sees biggest cost drop (~28%) because batching and prefetch hit more. long-context (>1024) p99 improved too but less cost delta (~10%).

samir: what changed exactly? I thought kv-prefetch only affects cache warmups.

maria: combo: adaptive KV-prefetch now preloads tail KV pages for sessions predicted to continue, + dynamic microbatcher that merges low-rt concurrent requests into sub-ms batches when SSE is idle. the microbatcher has a latency ceiling param (default 12ms) so tail latency stays bounded.

runtime-oncall: watched infra metrics during rollout: GPU mem stable, no OOMs, queue length spiked briefly during 50% step for ~40s then smoothed. we saw a couple of 429s at canary 5% from an older client variant (fixed by fallback policy).

ops: flagged for follow-up: please add a rule to the alerting playbook to fire if queue_length > 120 for >1m after a rollout.

maria: noted and added a quick alert patch (PR #4281). will link once merged.

jen: can we publish a short blurb for product and cs about expected latency/cost improvements (with caveats re: long-context)? they asked for clear numbers to share with customers.

maria: yes, drafting a one-pager. rough shareable bullet: "Typical customers: ~20-30% reduction in inference cost + ~20-30% reduction in p95 latency for short-context workloads. Results vary for long-context."

alex: attaching perf graph: https://internal.redwood/perf/graphs/1792345678 (internal only).

runtime-oncall: continuing watch. will keep this thread updated for 24h and revert if any regression at p99 > previous baseline.

samir: awesome work, team :tada: — can we add a short note to the release notes about the fallback policy change that prevented that 429? might save support tickets.

maria: yep will include it. thanks everyone for quick reviews and oncall support.

jen: adding small follow-up: can we run the same canary on dedicated pools next week? want to validate reserved capacity behavior under burst workloads.

maria: scheduled a dedicated run for Tue 09:00 PT. invite sent.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: commit b3f9c2a -> prod | status=success | duration=00:28:12 :rocket:
